name: zoteus
description: MCP server that gives Claude and other MCP clients access to a Zotero library: search, citations, adding items, safe writes, semantic search, and PDF passages.
long_description: Zoteus gives Claude complete, safe access to your Zotero library via the Web API v3 and the desktop local API: items, collections, tags, attachments, full-text, sync, groups, add-by-DOI/ISBN/PMID/arXiv, CSL bibliography formatting, hybrid semantic search, and an OpenAlex/Crossref scholarly graph.

api_key.title: Zotero API Key
api_key.description: Create one at https://www.zotero.org/settings/keys. Optional when the Zotero desktop app is running (key-free reads and personal-library writes); needed for sync, group libraries, and writes when the app is closed.

local.title: Zotero local API
local.description: Talk to the running Zotero desktop app (key-free reads, and writes where supported): auto | on | off.

embeddings.title: Semantic-search embeddings
embeddings.description: Embedding provider for semantic search: local (default, on-device model) | openai | gemini | off (keyword-only index: fastest to build, useful on slow machines).

embedding_model.title: Embedding model
embedding_model.description: Model used by the provider selected above, local included: Xenova/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 for local, text-embedding-3-small for openai, text-embedding-004 for gemini. For local embeddings this is any transformers.js feature-extraction model, which is how a German or otherwise multilingual library gets an embedder trained for it: Xenova/multilingual-e5-small (same 384 dimensions, weights downloaded once into the data directory, E5 query/passage prefixes applied for you). Vectors from two models are not comparable, so the index is dropped (with a notice) and has to be rebuilt after you change this. Leave empty to use the provider's own default.

embedding_dtype.title: Local embedding precision
embedding_dtype.description: Weight precision the on-device model loads at. Leave empty for fp32, the full-precision weights, which is what every index built so far holds. q8 loads the quantized file instead: Xenova/multilingual-e5-small downloads at 129 MB rather than 465 MB, which is what makes local multilingual search practical on a machine with a few gigabytes of RAM. This names a file the model's repository has to publish, not a conversion performed here: the Xenova mirrors publish the quantized variants, a model's own repository often publishes fp32 only, and asking for one that does not exist fails at load rather than falling back. Above fp32 the precision is part of the stored embedder identity, so the index is dropped (with a notice) and has to be rebuilt after you change this. Ignored when the provider above is openai or gemini.

embed_batch_size.title: Embedding batch size
embed_batch_size.description: Passages per embedding call: one API request, or one local pipeline call. Default 32. Lower it when a provider rejects a whole batch (OpenAI answers 400 above 300K tokens per request, a ceiling full-text passages reach far sooner than metadata ones). On a large full-text build against an API provider, use this with the pause below: 256 here and 8000 ms there held a 10,000-item library well under OpenAI's rate limit. Leave empty to keep the default.

embed_batch_delay_ms.title: Pause between embedding calls (ms)
embed_batch_delay_ms.description: Wait between embedding calls. Default 0, which only yields to the event loop, so the rate is set entirely by how fast the provider answers: on a large full-text build that lands at roughly the provider's tokens-per-minute ceiling whatever your tier, and every request there risks a 429. A rate-limited request now backs off and retries, and an interrupted build resumes rather than re-embedding, but 8000 ms here (with batch size 256 above) is what keeps a 10,000-item build clear of the limit outright. Leave empty to keep the default.

index_fulltext.title: Index PDF full text
index_fulltext.description: Also index the body text Zotero extracted from your PDFs, so semantic search can match a claim buried inside a paper and not just its title and abstract. Off by default because it is expensive: roughly 9x the passages, index size and embedding time. You can also turn it on for a single build with zotero_index fulltext:true. This build used to kill the extension partway through when run inside the Claude app (issue #37); it was the on-device embedding model asking for one block of memory bigger than the app will hand out, and Zoteus now embeds fewer passages per call in here, so the build runs to completion. It is a little slower in the app than in a terminal, and produces exactly the same index.

index_fulltext_max_chars.title: Full-text characters per item
index_fulltext_max_chars.description: How much of each item's extracted body text gets indexed when the setting above is on. The default, 40000 characters (roughly 13 pages of dense text), truncates long documents: only the beginning of a book or a long thesis is searchable. Set 0 for no cap and full coverage, at the cost of a bigger index and a longer build; this box will not display a 0 you type, but the value is saved and does take effect, so an empty-looking field after typing 0 is not a rejection. Type a very large number (10000000) instead if you would rather read back the value you set. Leave empty to keep the default.

index_max_items.title: Max items per index build
index_max_items.description: How many top-level items a single index build will crawl. Default 5000. Raise it for a library larger than that: a build that stops at the cap reports how many items it left unindexed, and semantic search repeats the warning. Leave empty to keep the default.

transformers_path.title: Local embeddings path
transformers_path.description: Where to find @huggingface/transformers for on-device (local) embeddings. This bundle cannot ship it: the resolved dependency tree, onnxruntime's native binaries included, is about 700 MB. Do not use `npm i -g`: Claude Desktop runs Zoteus on its own built-in Node, so a global install under nvm (or any version manager) lands next to a Node this extension never executes, and switching versions later breaks the path. Install it in a folder of its own instead: `mkdir -p ~/.zoteus-deps && cd ~/.zoteus-deps && npm init -y && npm i @huggingface/transformers`, then pick that folder's node_modules here (for example /home/you/.zoteus-deps/node_modules). Leave empty to run keyword-only (BM25) search, or pick openai/gemini above.

update_check.title: Check for updates
update_check.description: Once a day, ask GitHub whether a newer Zoteus release exists and mention it in zotero_whoami. A manually installed extension never auto-updates, so this is the only upgrade notice you get. Off by default: it is the one request Zoteus makes that you did not ask for. It sends no library content and no personal data.
